bullets.title: Fed delivers hawkish surprise: 9 members project 2026 hike, core PCE raised to 3.3%
bullets.body: Chair Warsh's maiden FOMC meeting held rates at 3.5–3.75% but dropped forward guidance entirely — the most hawkish statement in a year per NLP scoring. Nine of 18 participants project at least one hike in 2026 (6 project two or more); median 2026 core PCE revised up 0.8pp to 3.3%. Markets now pricing a full hike by October FOMC and 45bp+ of tightening by spring 2027; 2Y yields rose 11–13bp on the day. Warsh also announced 5 task forces on communications, balance sheet, data, productivity, and inflation framework, signaling a structural shift toward opacity and higher volatility.

bullets.title: US/Iran MoU signed — oil falls 2%+, Fed's inflation case potentially undermined
bullets.body: The US-Iran memorandum of understanding took effect overnight, with blockade lifting and oil-export waivers described as immediate rather than conditional. WTI fell ~2% to the mid-$70s, the lowest since the start of the war; Goldman projects 70% of Gulf exports normalize by month-end and production at pre-war levels by October. Jefferies flags a key macro wrinkle: >250M barrels of stranded Iranian and Gulf inventory could flood the market simultaneously, eroding the energy-driven inflation impulse that underpins the Fed's hawkish June dot plot — making current dots potentially backward-looking.

bullets.title: S&P futures +0.7–0.8% overnight; tape reverting to AI/semis demand narrative
bullets.body: Despite 85%+ of S&P 500 stocks closing lower Wednesday on hawkish FOMC and bond vol spike, futures recovered overnight (+0.81%) as the market pivoted back to AI capex momentum and the Intel-Apple chip deal. JPM flipped to tactically bullish, favoring Tech and maintaining a tactical long in Financials. SOXX ETF indicated +4.28% pre-market; NDX futures +1.46%. Retail single-stock purchases hit the 91st percentile with NVDA (+$567M), GOOGL (+$300M), and MSFT (+$265M) leading inflows.

bullets.title: Trump confirms Apple-Intel domestic chip deal; INTC surges 9–10% pre-market
bullets.body: Trump tweeted at 00:29 ET that Apple agreed to work with Intel to design and build chips in America; INTC traded +9–10% pre-open at ~$121. Intel simultaneously announced the start of risk production on its 18A-P node (9% better performance or 18% lower power vs. 18A). JPM notes the Apple-Intel collaboration was previously reported in May but the market is reacting with volume; TSM maintains a 2+ year process lead but INTC's domestic manufacturing narrative is driving incremental sentiment.

bullets.title: Memory chip inflation forces Apple price hikes; DRAM/NAND up 600–900% since 2023
bullets.body: Apple CEO Tim Cook confirmed product price increases are unavoidable as memory/storage costs have become 'unsustainable'; hyperscalers are consuming 50%+ of memory supply. WSJ analysis suggests iPhone Pro could see ~$270 price increases; Morgan Stanley forecasts a 15% chip supply deficit through 2027. Apple said it's willing to use its balance sheet to help expand memory supply but won't build its own fabs. Memory stocks (Samsung +5.5%, SK Hynix +7.5%) rallied 4–6% on the comments.

bullets.title: JPM raises WFE forecasts to +28% in 2026 and +29% in 2027 on AI capex surge
bullets.body: JPM lifted its CY2026 wafer fab equipment growth forecast from 21% to 28% YoY ($155B) and CY2027 from 18% to 29% ($200B), citing top-4 US CSP capex up ~80% YoY in 2026 and ~50% in 2027. China AI data center capex is forecast to roughly double from $55–69B in 2026 to $95–151B by 2029 (20–30% CAGR), with domestic GPU AI server sales of $34B/$48B/$79B in 2026/27/28. DRAM, TSMC, INTC/Samsung foundry, and YMTC cited as the biggest sources of WFE upside in absolute dollars.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler GPU capex entering $1T territory; GOOGL's $50/watt deal signals upward bias
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags Google renting ~110K GB300 GPUs at an estimated $50/watt annually as a bullish signal for GCP and AWS growth acceleration and META's neocloud opportunity. MS sees GCP/AWS monetization at $25/watt in 2027 driving 27%/16% upside to current growth estimates; META's 500MW neocloud capacity at $30/MW could add $4+ to 2028 EPS. Aggregate hyperscaler capex estimates are biased toward $1T in 2027.

bullets.title: Warsh Fed structurally more volatile for equities; 10Y yield -5bp to 4.45% but front-end hawkish
bullets.body: New Fed Chair Warsh deliberately dropped the dot plot from his own submission, shortened the statement, and established five reform task forces — signaling a shift to conditional, opaque policy. The 2Y yield touched 4.21% while the 10Y fell 5bp to 4.45%, with real yields rising 10bp at the 5-year point. JPM warns that reduced forward guidance will structurally raise volatility and term premium. Morgan Stanley's base case remains on hold for 2026, projecting core PCE at 3.0% vs. the Fed's 3.3%, contingent on oil relief from the Iran deal coming through.

bullets.title: ACN -14% on bookings miss and FY27 guidance implying negative organic growth
bullets.body: Accenture Q3 EPS beat ($3.80 vs $3.71) but revenue missed ($18.72B vs $18.78B consensus), new bookings fell 3% YoY to $19.3B (managed services missed badly at $9.06B vs $11.32B expected), and FY26 revenue growth guidance was cut to 3–4% from 3–5%. Jefferies notes the Street now models negative organic growth for FY27; ACN's multiple has de-rated to 15+ year lows. Weakness spread to IT services peers: CTSH -4.8%, IBM -4.7%, EPAM -4.2%, INFY -4.0%.

bullets.title: Mag7 de-risked Wednesday; semis saw strong dip-buying with +3z net demand
bullets.body: Hedge fund net leverage fell 4% to the 8th percentile on a 12-month basis Wednesday; Mag7 saw -2.3z selling and -0.8z short covering. However, semis reversed with strong net buying (+3z, +2z over two days). JPM warns that rising semiconductor stock volatility elevates VaR-shock risk and potential tantrums via forced selling. Financials ETFs were the most bought as % of AUM last week. MRVL index addition (S&P 500) expected to create index-related demand but could weigh on SPX mechanically.

bullets.title: KeyBanc CIO survey: IT budget growth below 3.5% in 2026; legacy SaaS faces headwinds
bullets.body: KeyBanc's CIO survey predicts 2026 IT budget growth will come in below 3.5%, with 2027 even softer — breaking a pattern of out-year optimism. Security budgets are expected to nearly double to 6%+; 34.5% of CIOs plan to reduce spend with legacy software vendors (Adobe, Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow) in favor of AI-native solutions. Over 60% of CIOs expect to exceed AI token/credit budgets, with AI consuming 6%+ of 2026 IT spend rising to 10%+ in 2027. Anthropic Claude predicted to jump from 3rd to 1st in enterprise AI rankings.

bullets.title: Databricks ARR surging to ~$6.9B (+80% YoY); expanding into SIEM, CDP, real-time OLAP
bullets.body: Databricks is on track to hit $6.9B ARR in F1H27 with core growth at 65% ex-token pass-through; AI-related revenue exceeds $1.7B run-rate growing >100% YoY. The company is now competing directly with Snowflake (LTAP architecture), Salesforce/Twilio (CustomerLake CDP), CRWD/PANW/DDOG (Panther/Lakewatch SIEM), and Clickhouse/MongoDB (Lakehouse//RT). Enterprises are migrating off Azure/Synapse/Snowflake/Palantir to Databricks for AI cost-efficiency; 86% of customers expect to increase spend over the next 12 months.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples compressed; IGV -14.2% YTD vs S&P +9.1% as AI-native disruption accelerates
bullets.body: The Wolfe All-SaaS index trades at 5.0x FY+2 EV/Sales and declined 4.63% week-over-week; IGV is down 14.2% YTD against the S&P 500's +9.1% gain. The All-Security index trades at 7.5x FY+2 and declined 2.16% WoW. CIOs flagging intent to cut legacy vendor spend in favor of AI-native solutions is a structural headwind for the group. The fiscal impulse is also set to reverse from a +0.55% GDP contribution in Q2 2026 to a -0.5% drag in Q2–Q3 2027.

bullets.title: Retail spending decelerated sharply in June week 2; traffic tracker shows Q2 well below Q1
bullets.body: KeyBanc credit/debit card data shows all-retail spending growth slowed to +1.2% for the week of June 14, down from +5.3% the prior week and below the 6-week average of +3.4%. Citi's traffic tracker confirms Q2TD deceleration to +1.0% vs Q1's +3.4%, with notable weakness at FIVE (-960bp), ASO (-650bp), GAP (-600bp), and ANF (-500bp). Consumer staples (XLP) underperformed the S&P by 234bp this week, its 7th underperformance in 12 weeks, with lower-income consumer pressure from gas prices cited as a key driver.

bullets.title: Geopolitical de-escalation: US-Iran deal plus G7 Russia/critical minerals alignment
bullets.body: Beyond the oil impact, the Iran MoU removes a significant geopolitical risk premium. G7 leaders separately agreed on increased Ukraine air defense/long-range capabilities, potential Patriot production licensing in Ukraine, and a multilateral critical minerals strategy targeting no single country supplying >60% of rare earth imports by 2030 — directly targeting Chinese dependency. Trump also signaled possible USMCA termination, a tail risk for auto and cross-border supply chains.

bullets.title: Microsoft building major AI business with Chinese firms; MSFT/ByteDance on track for $1B+/yr
bullets.body: Bloomberg reports ByteDance is on track to spend over $1B annually on Microsoft AI and cloud services; Ant Group, Meituan, and Tencent are also significant Azure AI customers. OpenAI has complained privately to Microsoft about insufficient safeguards against model copying. Separately, a top Alphabet AI researcher (Noam Shazeer, Gemini co-lead) is departing for OpenAI as AI architecture lead — the latest in a string of talent moves with 85+ ex-Salesforce employees also having moved to Anthropic/OpenAI this year.

bullets.title: UK labor market slightly better than expected; BoE tightening bias intact
bullets.body: UK unemployment unexpectedly fell to 4.9% in the three months to April (from 5.0%), though private sector payroll growth is running at 5.7% annualized — keeping underlying wage pressures sticky. BoE is expected to maintain its tightening bias with rate hikes probable in H2 2026. UK CPI came in at a second consecutive downside surprise (2.8% vs. 3.3% forecast), but the BoE is not yet ready to turn dovish; Norges Bank separately held at 4.25% but raised its 4Q rate path by 20bp, implying a September hike.

bullets.title: Energy sector: oil structurally lower; data center and LNG themes dominating investor attention
bullets.body: WTI is now back in the mid-$70s ($74.58), with Goldman projecting Gulf exports at pre-war levels by October; BofA cut its Brent forecast to $82/bbl for 2026 (from $93) and $70 for 2027. JPM's energy conference attendance data is telling: most-requested meetings are VST, WMB, BKR, and TLN — not traditional E&Ps — reflecting investor pivot toward power, LNG, and data center power themes. GS initiated TLN at Buy with a $499 PT, citing AWS PPA de-risking and structural PJM supply-demand tightening.

bullets.title: China AI capex doubling by 2029; domestic memory shift from Samsung/Micron to CXMT/YMTC
bullets.body: JPM forecasts China AI data center capex expanding from $55–69B in 2026 to $95–151B by 2029, with domestic GPU AI server sales growing 41%/65% in 2027/28. Chinese memory buyers are actively shifting from Samsung and Micron toward domestic suppliers CXMT and YMTC. SK Hynix has begun shipping HBM4E samples (16Gbps/pin, 48GB, 20% better power efficiency than HBM4), maintaining ~58% HBM market share vs Samsung's 21%. Samsung Foundry is meanwhile winning new orders from GOOGL (Axion CPUs), AMD (future CPUs), and Tesla (AI6 chips).
